trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.

Going around the edge to (2,1) would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going down would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number (and 1 more option fails too). So the line goes up.
Number 2 is only reachable this way.
The line must go down: left is number 12, which comes later; around the edge to (5,4) is number 5, which comes later.
Going down, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,4); going left, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes right.
Going right would leave number 5 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes down.
I can't rule out down or left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: down.
Going left, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,1). So the line goes right.
Number 6 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Cell (3,5) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes around the edge to (3,1).
Going up would leave number 8 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes down.
Going right would leave both cell (3,2) and cell (4,3) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes down.
The line must go right: around the edge to (1,1) is number 10, which comes later.

Going up would leave both cell (3,2) and cell (4,3) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going right would leave number 9 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes around the edge to (1,2).
Number 10 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
I grow a search tree: my policy network suggests moves, a trained value head judge them. 40 simulations per move.
One of my simulated futures reached the end after 8 simulations. Following it!
Let evolution do the work: 24 random lines compete, the fittest breed and mutate.
Generation 0: the best random line covers 10/25 cells (40%).
Generation 1: fitness 25/25. The best line covers 25 cells.
Generation 1: a perfect line evolved! Every cell covered.
Feeling lucky! Before every move I'll play 24 random futures and bet on the move that survives most often.
Jackpot! A future after going up covers the whole board. Cashing in!
Let x(cell, step) mean 'this cell is step number <step> of the line'. 25 cells x 25 steps, minus everything that's impossible at a glance.
Encoded 1,405 variables and 3,824 clauses in 0.00 s (397 position variables survive the pruning).
Solver found a model in 0.00 s. Decoding it into a line...
Q.E.D. Every clause is satisfied.
